title: Attention heads: MHA, MQA, GQA and MLA
question: How do independent, shared, grouped and latent key/value representations change retrieval and retained state?
prerequisites: Vectors, matrix multiplication, a model parameter, and the role of a loss. No Python syntax course.
The single-head projections, stable softmax and causal rule from Attention Foundations.

chapters.title: Multi-query attention: many questions, one stored memory
Grouped-query attention: choose who shares memory

practice.question: After concatenating two scalar head outputs, does W_O mix tokens or head features?
practice.answer: It mixes head-feature channels separately at each token. Token-to-token mixing already occurred inside each attention head. In our first row, [1,1] multiplied by the declared W_O becomes [0.5,1.5]. Multiple heads allow different distributions but do not guarantee unique linguistic roles.
practice.rubric: Identify the feature contraction and reproduce the small output-projection calculation.

practice.question: Why is [B,T,H,d_h] the wrong layout for Q @ K.transpose(-2,-1)?
practice.answer: Its last two axes are heads and features. That product compares heads for each token, producing [B,T,H,H]. Transposing to [B,H,T,d_h] makes the contraction produce [B,H,T,T], one token-by-token score matrix per head and sequence. Merging outputs also requires restoring token/head order, not merely matching element counts.
practice.rubric: Name the query-token and source-token axes before multiplication and the feature order after merging.

practice.question: Does packing query/key/value projections implement GQA or reduce the count of stored KV heads?
practice.answer: No. Our packed MHA preserves separate Q/K/V parameters per head and H_q=H_kv. GQA deliberately shares key/value heads among query heads, which needs an explicit grouping rule and corresponding correctness checks. Neither packing nor grouping automatically removes the sequence-length cost of the score calculation.
practice.rubric: Separate an equivalent tensor layout from a changed head-sharing relationship.

practice.question: If every head uses the same K and V, must its output be identical?
practice.answer: No. Distinct query vectors can give distinct score rows, softmax distributions and value mixtures. Equal queries and masks would give equal retrievals. Shared memory alone does not force equal queries.
practice.rubric: Explain the roles of Q versus K/V and use the scalar example.

practice.question: At fixed head width, what happens when eight query heads share one KV head instead of eight?
practice.answer: The retained KV payload becomes one eighth as large. The query-head count remains eight; score calculations still exist for all eight. This is an architectural restriction, not a guarantee of unchanged pretrained-MHA outputs or eightfold wall-clock speed.
practice.rubric: Separate stored bytes, operation count, model behavior and measured latency.

practice.question: For eight query heads and two contiguous KV groups, which KV head does query head 5 use?
practice.answer: Each group contains four query heads. floor(5/4)=1, so query head 5 uses KV head 1 in zero-based indexing. It must not be assigned by h mod G for this mapping.
practice.rubric: State the indexing convention and the complete grouping rule.

practice.question: Does mean-pooling an arbitrary pretrained MHA checkpoint into GQA preserve all outputs?
practice.answer: No. Sharing reduces independent K/V parameters, and softmax does not commute with averaging. Uptraining/evaluation is separate from the exact identity between grouped and expanded execution of an already specified GQA.
practice.rubric: Distinguish architecture conversion from equivalent execution and explain nonlinearity.

practice.question: Can you average MHA heads and call the result an exact MLA conversion?
practice.answer: No. Absorption is exact inside a specified factorized model; choosing a low-rank bottleneck constrains the coefficients and requires separate adaptation/evaluation.
practice.rubric: Distinguish architecture approximation from algebraic associativity.

practice.question: For B=1,T=10,r=4,dr=2,float32, what is retained per layer?
practice.answer: 10*(4+2)*4=240 bytes of latent plus positional-key payload. Queries are not retained; metadata is additional.
practice.rubric: Include the positional key and distinguish payload from allocation.
